title: Rest and Motion: Motion is Relative
subject: Physics
objective: Are you moving right now? It depends on who is watching. Rest and motion are always measured from a reference point.

fill.q: An object is at rest if its position does not change with ____ relative to a reference point.
The fixed point used to describe position is called the ____ point.
A passenger in a moving bus is at ____ relative to the bus and in ____ relative to the road.
Nothing on the Earth is in ____ rest, because the Earth itself moves.

tf.q: An object can be at rest and in motion at the same time.
tf.explain: Yes, for two different reference points.

tf.q: A parked car is at rest relative to the Sun.
tf.explain: The car moves with the Earth around the Sun.

tf.q: Two trains moving side by side at the same speed are at rest relative to each other.
tf.explain: The distance between them does not change.

tf.q: We can say whether something moves without choosing a reference point.
tf.explain: Rest and motion have meaning only relative to a reference point.

ar.a: A person sleeping in a moving train is in motion.
ar.r: Motion is described relative to a reference point.
ar.explain: Relative to the ground the sleeper changes position, and the reason (reference point) is exactly why.

ar.a: A tree is always at rest.
ar.r: A tree does not change its position relative to the ground.
ar.explain: A is false: relative to a moving bus or the Sun the tree moves. R is true.

mcq.q: A girl sits in a moving car. Relative to the car she is:
mcq.explain: Her position inside the car does not change.

mcq.q: A roadside tree appears to move backward to a bus passenger. This shows:
mcq.explain: Relative to the bus the tree's position changes.

mcq.q: Which is at rest relative to the Earth's surface?
mcq.explain: Its position on the ground does not change.

mcq.q: To decide whether an object moves, first choose:
mcq.explain: Motion is always relative to a reference point.

short.q: Define rest and motion. Why must a reference point be named?
short.solution: Rest: position unchanged with time relative to a reference point; motion: position changes. The same object can be at rest for one observer and moving for another, so the statement is incomplete without the reference point.

short.q: A ball is thrown up inside a train moving at constant speed. Describe its path for a passenger and for a person on the platform.
short.solution: For the passenger it goes straight up and down. For the person on the platform it also moves forward with the train, so its path is a curve.

left: Passenger seen from inside the bus

match.explain: The passenger keeps the same place in the bus but changes place relative to the road; the Earth's own motion rules out absolute rest.
